item: Path A - Medi-Cal (if MAGI at or below 138% FPL)
detail: No earned income needed, no asset test, no premium; apply any time of year. From January 1, 2027, expansion adults must also satisfy the work and community engagement rule for a qualifying month - in California, any one month since the last determination at renewal (or the month before application for new applicants). It can be met with $0 earned income via MAGI-based monthly income of at least $580 from any source (including net rental, interest, trading gains), 80 hours of structured community service, at least half-time school, a work program, a combination, or an exemption. Warning: losing Medi-Cal for noncompliance does not unlock subsidized Covered California coverage (full cost only).
source_name: DHCS - Eligibility by Federal Poverty Level
notes: Income limits rise with household size - see the Medi-Cal page. Qualifying-month and subsidy-bar rules: AB 2161 / MEDIL I26-25 (Work Requirements page).

item: Path B - Covered California with federal premium tax credit (MAGI 138-400% FPL)
value: 400% FPL = $63,840/year for one person (2027 coverage, 2026 guidelines)
detail: No work requirement at all; premium tax credit lowers the monthly premium for households 100-400% FPL; Silver plan cost-sharing reductions up to 250% FPL; California state subsidy up to 200% FPL for 2027. Open enrollment November 1, 2026 - January 31, 2027.
notes: Excess advance credit must now be repaid in full if income is underestimated (from tax year 2026).

detail: Full-price Covered California or off-exchange plans; the California state subsidy is limited to households up to 200% FPL; the state individual mandate penalty applies if you go uninsured without an exemption (at least $950/adult or 2.5% of gross income over the filing threshold).
notes: See the Covered California page for the penalty and its exemptions.

value: Emergency stabilization always available; hospital charity care for patients at or below 400% FPL
detail: EMTALA requires Medicare-participating hospitals to screen and stabilize emergency conditions regardless of ability to pay; California Health and Safety Code 127405 requires hospitals to maintain charity care and discount payment policies for uninsured or high-medical-cost patients at or below 400% FPL.
notes: Not a substitute for coverage; see the Other Options page.

item: Path E - If age 65+ or qualifying disability
detail: Medicare covers people 65 or older (and some younger people with disability, ESRD, or ALS); a 7-month initial enrollment period surrounds the 65th birthday. People entitled to or enrolled in Medicare are not subject to the Medicaid work requirement.

item: Path F - If recently in a W-2 job with benefits
detail: COBRA lets workers and families keep employer group coverage temporarily (generally 18 months after job loss or reduced hours, up to 36 months for other qualifying events) at up to 102% of the full premium.
notes: Full-cost COBRA is often more expensive than subsidized marketplace coverage.
